Bill number: HB1740
<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1740

 By Glynn

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to the Individualized Education Act.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1402(3), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (3) "Eligible student" means a resident of this state who:

 (A)

 (i) Is a child with any of the following disabilities as defined by the

 state board of education pursuant to § 49-10-102:

 (a) Autism;

 (b) Deaf-blindness;

 (c) Hearing impairments;

 (d) Intellectual disability;

 (e) Orthopedic impairments;

 (f) Traumatic brain injury;

 (g) Visual impairments;

 (h) Developmental delay;

 (i) Multiple disabilities;

 (j) A specific learning disability; or

 (k) Deafness;

 (ii) Has an active individualized education program (IEP) in

 accordance with 34 C.F.R. § 300 et seq., § 49-10-102, and regulations of

 the state board of education with one (1) of the disabilities pursuant to

 subdivision (3)(A)(i) as the primary or secondary disability in effect at the

 time the department receives the request for participation in the program;

 and

 (iii) Meets at least one (1) of the following requirements:

 (a) Was previously enrolled in and attended a Tennessee

 public school for the one (1) full school year immediately

 preceding the school year in which the student receives an

 individualized education account (IEA);

 (b) Is enrolling in a Tennessee school for the first time; or

 (c) Received an individualized education account (IEA) in

 the previous school year; or

 (B)

 (i) Is a child with a medical condition that inhibits the child from

 attending school in person, as determined by the state board of

 education; and

 (ii) Is entitled to attend a public school;

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1402(6), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (6) "Participating school" means:

 (A) A nonpublic school that meets the requirements established in this

 part and seeks to enroll eligible students; or

 (B) For an eligible student, as defined in subdivision (3)(B), a home

 school, as defined in § 49-6-3050(a)(1);

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1404, is amended by adding

the following as a new subsection:

 (d) This section does not apply to an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-

 1402(3)(B), or a participating school, as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(B).

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1403(d), is amended by

adding ", as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(A)," after "A participating school".

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1405(a)(7), is amended by

adding ", as defined in § 49-10-1402(6)(A)," after "of participating schools".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 10, Part 14, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) A parent of an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), shall ensure

 that funds in an IEA are used only for approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b).

 (b) The department shall create and implement a process to ensure that funds in

 an IEA for an eligible student, as defined in § 49-10-1402(3)(B), are regularly monitored

 to ensure compliance with this section and § 49-10-1403(b).

 (c) The department may suspend or terminate an eligible student from

 participating in the program, if the department determines that the parent has failed to

 comply with the requirements of this section. If the department terminates an eligible

 student's participation in the program pursuant to this subsection (c), then the student is

 ineligible from participating in the program in the future.

 SECTION 7. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change who can take part in Tennessee's individualized education account (IEA) program. It would add a second group of eligible students and set rules for how their accounts are used and monitored.

The bill rewrites the definition of "eligible student" in two parts. The first group is children with an active individualized education program (IEP) who have one of these disabilities as a primary or secondary disability: autism, deaf-blindness, hearing impairments, intellectual disability, orthopedic impairments, traumatic brain injury, visual impairments, developmental delay, multiple disabilities, a specific learning disability, or deafness. The IEP must be in effect when the department receives the request to participate. The student must also meet one of three conditions. The student was enrolled in and attended a Tennessee public school for the full prior school year. Or the student is enrolling in a Tennessee school for the first time. Or the student received an IEA in the previous school year.

The second group is Tennessee resident children who have a medical condition that keeps them from attending school in person, as determined by the state board of education, and who are entitled to attend public school.

The bill also changes the definition of "participating school." It would still include a nonpublic school that meets the program's requirements and seeks to enroll eligible students. For students in the medical-condition group, it would also include a home school as defined in a cited statute. The bill adds cross-references so that some existing provisions about participating schools apply only to nonpublic schools. A new subsection says the existing section 49-10-1404 does not apply to medical-condition students or to home schools.

A new section sets rules for parents of medical-condition students. The parent must make sure IEA funds are used only for the approved expenses listed in § 49-10-1403(b). The department must create and carry out a process to regularly monitor these accounts for compliance. The department may suspend or terminate a student's participation if it finds the parent did not comply. A student who is terminated would be ineligible to take part in the future.

The act would take effect July 1, 2026.
</summary>

assessments.rationale: Conveys the disability list, active IEP requirement, primary-or-secondary designation, and timing, but omits Tennessee residency for this route and the governing state-board disability definitions and IEP standards.

assessments.summary_quote: The student must also meet one of three conditions. The student was enrolled in and attended a Tennessee public school for the full prior school year. assessments.rationale: Conveys all three alternative enrollment/history conditions for the disability-based route.

assessments.summary_quote: The second group is Tennessee resident children who have a medical condition that keeps them from attending school in person, as determined by the state board of education, and who are entitled to attend public school.
assessments.rationale: Identifies a separate eligibility route with residency, a board-determined medical condition affecting in-person attendance, and public-school entitlement, without imposing the first route's conditions.

assessments.summary_quote: It would still include a nonpublic school that meets the program's requirements and seeks to enroll eligible students. For students in the medical-condition group, it would also include a home school as defined in a cited statute.
assessments.rationale: Conveys both participating-school categories and limits home-school inclusion to medical-condition students.

assessments.summary_quote: A new subsection says the existing section 49-10-1404 does not apply to medical-condition students or to home schools.
assessments.rationale: Identifies the exempted section and both exempt categories, with participating home schools established by the preceding context.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill adds cross-references so that some existing provisions about participating schools apply only to nonpublic schools.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the restriction to nonpublic schools but does not identify § 49-10-1403(d) and § 49-10-1405(a)(7), which are necessary to identify the affected provisions.

assessments.rationale: Conveys the parent's duty, the medical-condition scope, and the restriction to the specified approved expenses.

assessments.summary_quote: The department must create and carry out a process to regularly monitor these accounts for compliance.
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory creation and implementation of regular monitoring; the preceding context identifies the medical-condition accounts and approved-expense requirements.

assessments.summary_quote: The department may suspend or terminate a student's participation if it finds the parent did not comply.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the department's discretionary suspension or termination authority upon a finding of parental noncompliance with the new rules.

assessments.summary_quote: A student who is terminated would be ineligible to take part in the future.
assessments.rationale: Conveys permanent future ineligibility following termination under the new section.
